Adds numeric-gloss 3 and collective trā-i to specific *trāyaḥ subsection. Compare Tirahi trā and Palula trō. Perder identifies collective -i; excludes coordinated trā-o until composition review.

assignments.Notes: Adds numeric-gloss 3 and collective trā-i to specific *trāyaḥ subsection. Compare Tirahi trā and Palula trō. Perder identifies collective -i; excludes coordinated trā-o until composition review.
Adds survey 4 to catúraḥ subsection, as for accepted Dameli cōr. Compare Pashai čōr, Gawarbati ċūr and Palula čūr; survey retroflex transcription preserved.
Adds survey 5 to pañca family. Compare Gawarbati pōnċ and Nuristani Ashkun ponċ, Kati puč. Transcription variant of accepted Dameli pā̃c; no borrowing claim.
Adds survey 6 to specific *ṣuvaṭ subsection, not undifferentiated ṣaṣ. Compare Gawarbati ṣō and Nuristani Ashkun ṣu, Kati/Waigali ṣū.
Adds survey 7 to sapta family. Compare Pali satta, Kalasha sat and Nuristani Kati sut, Ashkun sot. Excludes Decker satʰaṣṭʰ seven as a mixed/problematic response.

Adds survey 8 to aṣṭā/aṣṭau family; compare Kalasha aṣṭ and Palula aṣṭ. Nuristani Kati uṣṭ and Waigali ōṣṭ are parallels that Turner regards as probable Dardic loans, not evidence of Nuristani-to-Dameli borrowing. Excludes nõ eight mismatch.
Adds survey 9 to nava family. Compare Pali nava and Nuristani Ashkun no, Prasun nū. Excludes survey nõ eight with inconsistent gloss.
Adds survey 10 to daśa family; compare Pali dasa, Gawarbati dɔš. Excludes Perder daś hand; ten and hand are distinct etymologies despite surface overlap.
Adds survey 11 to ekādaśa family. Compare Gawarbati ǰāš and Nuristani Waigali yāš. Perder treats 11 as synchronically monomorphemic, so no modern one-plus-ten component analysis.
Adds survey 12 to dvādaśa main section. Compare Gawarbati bāš, Palula bāš and Nuristani Waigali bāš. Perder treats it as synchronically monomorphemic.
Adds survey 14 to caturdaśa main section. Compare Palula čandēš and Nuristani Waigali čadēš. Nasal in Dameli directly supported by Turner; survey retroflex transcription retained.

Adds survey 15 to pañcadaśa family. Compare Palula panǰēš and Nuristani Waigali pačīš. Perder p. 88 explicitly connects the historical formation with five and ten, but treats the modern word as monomorphemic.
